```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(jsdiffr)
```

`jsdiffr` is a faithful R port of the
[jsdiff](https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff) JavaScript library. It computes the
difference between two pieces of text (or two sequences) using Myers' O(ND)
algorithm, implemented in C++ for speed on large inputs.

## The basics

Every diff function takes two inputs and returns a `data.table` of *change
objects* with four columns: `value`, `added`, `removed`, and `count`.

```{r}
d <- diff_chars("the quick brown fox", "the quiet brown ox")
d
as.data.frame(d)
```

You can diff at several granularities:

```{r}
diff_words("The quick brown fox", "The slow brown fox")
diff_lines("alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n", "alpha\nBETA\ngamma\n")
diff_sentences("Hello world. Foo bar.", "Hello world. Baz bar.")
```

`diff_arrays()` compares arbitrary sequences; its `value` column is a list of
the sub-sequences for each change:

```{r}
da <- diff_arrays(c("a", "b", "c"), c("a", "c", "d"))
da$value
```

## Diffing columns

Every string diff function is also vectorised, so it can be used as a column
in a `data.frame` or `data.table`. Two vectors of equal length (or one vector
and one length-1 value, which is recycled) are diffed element by element, and
each pair is rendered to a single string:

```{r}
library(data.table)

dt <- data.table(iris)
head(dt[, .(blah = diff_chars(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width), Species)], 4)
```

Non-character columns are coerced with `as.character()`, and `NA` on either
side gives `NA` out. Two length-1 strings still return a `jsdiff_changes`
table, as above.

`format` chooses the rendering. `"added"` and `"removed"` give only the
inserted or deleted text, which is often what you want for summarising a
column rather than displaying it:

```{r}
addr <- data.table(
  old = c("12 Smith St, Carlton", "9/4 Brown Rd, Fitzroy", "71 Lygon Street"),
  new = c("12 Smith Street, Carlton", "9/4 Browne Rd, Fitzroy", "71 Lygon Street")
)

addr[, .(changes = diff_words(old, new),
         added   = diff_words(old, new, format = "added"),
         removed = diff_words(old, new, format = "removed"))]
```

The other options are `"ansi"` (the coloured console form, best used with
`cat()`), `"html"`, `"xml"`, and `"changes"` for a list column of the full
change tables. `changes_to_markup()` is the renderer behind the default, and
its markers are configurable via the `jsdiffr.markup_add` and
`jsdiffr.markup_remove` options. See `help("vectorised-diffs")` for the
details.

The diff is computed once per *distinct* pair of values, so repeated pairs in
a long column cost almost nothing.

## Printing and colours

Printing a diff in an interactive console shows additions in green and deletions
in red. You can force this on or off:

```{r}
cat(format(diff_words("the cat sat", "the dog sat"), color = FALSE), "\n")
```

A diff rendered into a column is plain-text markup rather than colour, and that
is not a cosmetic choice: `print.data.table()` and `print.data.frame()` hand
their formatted cells to `print.default()`, which escapes the ESC byte of an
ANSI colour sequence. A coloured cell would print as the literal text
`\033[31mcat\033[0m` in any terminal.

Colour therefore needs a printer of its own. `diff_print()` formats the table
itself and writes it with `cat()`, measuring each cell by its *visible* width so
that the (zero-width) colour sequences do not pull the columns apart:

```{r}
diff_print(head(dt[, .(blah = diff_chars(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width), Species)], 4))
```

Colour is off here because this vignette is not a terminal, so the markers are
left in place; at a console the same call prints the deletions in red and the
insertions in green instead. `diff_print()` also takes a `data.frame`, a markup
column on its own, and a list column from `format = "changes"`.

To avoid wrapping every call, `diff_print_auto()` defines `print.data.table()`
and `print.data.frame()` in the global environment - which is what takes
precedence when the console auto-prints - sending tables that contain diff
markup to `diff_print()` and everything else to the method that would otherwise
have run:

```r
diff_print_auto()
dt[, .(blah = diff_chars(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width), Species)]  # coloured
diff_print_auto(FALSE)                                          # undo
```

`markup_to_ansi()` is the piece underneath, for when you want to colour a
markup column and print it yourself with `cat()`.

## Patches

The full unified-diff patch suite is available:

```{r}
old <- "line one\nline two\nline three\n"
new <- "line one\nline 2\nline three\nline four\n"
patch <- create_patch("example.txt", old, new)
cat(patch)
```

Patches can be parsed, applied, reversed, and re-formatted:

```{r}
identical(apply_patch(old, patch), new)

reversed <- format_patch(reverse_patch(parse_patch(patch)))
identical(apply_patch(new, reversed), old)
```

`apply_patch()` supports fuzzy matching via `fuzz_factor` and automatically
reconciles Unix/Windows line endings.

## HTML output for Shiny / R Markdown

`diff_to_html()` renders a diff as HTML spans you can drop into a Shiny app or
report. Pair it with `diff_css_default()` for styling.

```{r}
html <- diff_to_html(diff_words("the cat sat", "the dog sat"))
substr(html, 1, 120)
```

In a Shiny app:

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(tags$style(HTML(diff_css_default()))),
  uiOutput("diff")
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$diff <- renderUI({
    HTML(diff_to_html(diff_lines(old_text(), new_text())))
  })
}
```

## Converters

Changes can be serialised to XML or to Google's diff-match-patch format:

```{r}
convert_changes_to_xml(diff_chars("abc", "abd"))
str(convert_changes_to_dmp(diff_chars("abc", "abd")))
```

## Differences from jsdiff

* The API uses `snake_case`; `camelCase` aliases (`diffChars`, `createPatch`,
  ...) are provided for users porting JavaScript code.
* There is no asynchronous `callback` mode; the universal `max_edit_length` and
  `timeout` options are supported.
* `diff_words()`'s `intlSegmenter` option is not supported (R has no
  `Intl.Segmenter`).
```
